For embedded/5G firmware engineers, timely kernel updates are essential to patch security vulnerabilities and improve stability in RAN stack implementations. Immediate upgrade is recommended to maintain system integrity in production deployments.

title: [$] Fixing the TCMalloc regression with RSEQ operations
summary: A kernel regression in version 6.19 broke TCMalloc allocator due to changes in restartable sequences (RSEQ), a lockless user-space synchronization mechanism that firmware code relies on for performance-critical sections. Embedded developers using memory allocators in high-frequency 5G signal processing pipelines must understand RSEQ behavior and validate allocator compatibility to prevent subtle race conditions and preemption-related failures.

title: DirectX Support Promoted To Official Target Within LLVM

Microsoft has backed the initiative for being able to lower LLVM IR into the DirectX Intermediate Language (DXIL) for execution by Windows DirectX 12 graphics drivers. title: AI Made A Lot Of "Hideous" Code But Found Major Bottlenecks For Faster Linux Compilation
summary: An ARM Linux engineer used LLMs to identify parallelization bottlenecks in the Linux kernel build process, significantly speeding up compilation times despite the AI-generated code being messy.

title: Interface-Aware KV Cache Quantization for Dense On-Chip NVM in Long-Context LLM Decoding
summary: This paper proposes interface-aware KV cache quantization designed to store KV caches in dense on-chip non-volatile memory, removing off-chip bandwidth bottlenecks during long-context LLM decoding.
raw_snippet:
arXiv:2609.05764v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The key-value (KV) cache is the dominant memory bottleneck in long-context large language model (LLM) decoding: every step reads it entirely, so decoding is memory-bandwidth bound. Holding a quantized KV cache in dense on-chip non-volatile memory (NVM) removes the off-chip transfer. title: WIP: Energy-Efficient LLM-Based Serving Cluster Formulation in Cell-Free Massive MIMO
summary: This work addresses 6G network energy efficiency through User-Centric Cell-Free Massive MIMO architecture, proposing intelligent serving cluster selection algorithms to optimize which base stations serve each user. For 5G RAN firmware engineers, this represents a shift toward distributed processing models that reduce fronthaul overhead and backhaul load, requiring changes to DU/RU coordination logic and resource allocation algorithms in real-time baseband processing.

title: SDN-Orchestrated Dual-Path 5G/SATCOM Maritime Communications for Carrier Strike Groups
summary: The paper presents an SDN/SDR integrated framework combining 5G and satellite links with dynamic failover capabilities, demonstrating practical network orchestration for mission-critical communications with variable link quality. This directly impacts embedded firmware design for RAN elements handling heterogeneous connectivity, requiring adaptive modulation/coding schemes and dynamic resource scheduling to manage dual-path redundancy in real-time.

Abstract: Carrier Strike Group (CSG) communications must sustain mission traffic across heterogeneous links whose quality varies with distance, weather, fading, and intermittent outages. We present an integrated Software-Defined Networking (SDN)/Software-Defined Radio (SDR) framework that unifies 5G and satellite communications (SATCOM) under a single control plane for dual-path failover in CSG communications. title: Semantic Communication for Distributed Spectrum Monitoring over Unreliable Links
summary: This work proposes semantic communication techniques for distributed spectrum monitoring where sensor reports must traverse unreliable channels, addressing the fundamental problem of efficiently aggregating spectrum state information across multiple receivers. For 5G RAN firmware, this introduces compression and prioritization strategies for spectrum sensing data that reduce backhaul overhead while maintaining detection accuracy in distributed monitoring architectures.

Abstract: Distributed spectrum monitoring relies on spatially separated receivers to infer the state of the radio environment. A central task is to determine how many emitters are active and where they are located. title: AutoUVM: Automated Prefetching Framework for LLMs under UVM Oversubscription
summary: AutoUVM is an automated prefetching framework designed to reduce page-fault latency during LLM execution under GPU Unified Virtual Memory oversubscription without requiring manual CUDA modifications.
raw_snippet:
arXiv:2609.06172v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly exceed the memory capacity of commodity GPUs, making memory oversubscription common in practical deployments. NVIDIA Unified Virtual Memory (UVM) provides transparent access to host memory, but its page-fault-driven migrations introduce severe performance overhead. title: DejaVu: Unifying Memory Allocations to Eliminate Redundant Copies on Unified-Memory SoCs
summary: This paper identifies and eliminates unnecessary CPU-GPU memory copies on unified-memory systems by optimizing memory allocation strategies, targeting the inefficient discrete-GPU abstraction pattern that persists on edge platforms. For 5G RAN embedded engineers, this optimization directly improves energy efficiency and latency in GPU-accelerated baseband processing on edge RAN nodes, reducing wasted memory bandwidth in real-time signal processing pipelines.
raw_snippet:
arXiv:2609.05635v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: GPU applications on unified-memory (UMA) edge platforms often inherit a discrete-GPU memory abstraction in which they allocate one buffer for the CPU, another for the GPU, and copy data between them before and after GPU execution. On UMA hardware these buffers reside in the same physical DRAM, so the copies consume bandwidth, time, and energy without moving data across a physical boundary. title: Towards Continuous Profiling and Optimization of Quantum-Classical Pipelines
